title: Iran war: Iran targets a US radar in Bahrain and Kuwait reports drone attacks; the US strikes Qeshm Island
seoTitle: Iran war latest: Bahrain, Kuwait attacks and US strike on Qeshm
dek: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they hit a US-operated radar in Bahrain on 17 November, their third drone attack on Bahrain in five days. The US struck a missile launch site on Qeshm Island hours later, and Kuwait says it intercepted drones. There is still no peace deal.
happened: On 17 November Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its drones carried out a "precision operation" against a US-operated radar at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. US Central Command said the drones "were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or personnel". Al Jazeera counts it as Iran's third drone attack on Bahrain in five days, after a lull of several weeks. Hours later US jets struck what a US official called an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, in response to the attack on the US base. Early on 18 November Bahrain's military said it intercepted further Iranian attacks, and Kuwait's army said its air defences were responding to "hostile drone attacks". No casualties were reported in these attacks. At sea, Iran's armed forces said three oil tankers struck mines in the strait on 17 November; on 16 November the Panama-flagged Tara Gas was hit twice off Khasab, Oman, and India's ports minister said one Indian sailor was missing.

sides.says: The IRGC framed the Bahrain strike as a response to "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones". Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Hormozgan province, told the state news agency IRNA: "The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas." Iran restricts shipping through the strait to routes it has authorised.

US officials said the Qeshm strike responded to Iranian attacks on US personnel and assets. The US blockades Iranian ports and escorts tankers, and says it has cleared the main routes of mines; a third aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the region on 16 November. RFE/RL reports Trump has said he may hold off renewed large-scale strikes if talks continue, and has also suggested a deal is no longer necessary because the war has already been won.

Bahrain's military said it "confronted, intercepted, and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks" and later gave the all-clear. Kuwait's army said "any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting hostile attacks". Reuters linked the attacks on Bahrain to a Bahraini court sentencing 64 people, mostly Shia clerics, to life in prison for allegedly colluding with Iran.

Qatar's spokesman Majed Al Ansari said talks with Iranian officials on 17 November aimed at "bridging perspectives and narrowing the gap between proposals". Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi discussed shipping safety with Oman's foreign minister in Muscat. Analyst Andreas Krieg told AFP the attacks look like "deliberate testing of boundaries rather than an immediate return to full-scale warfare".

next: There is no comprehensive peace deal; all-out air strikes have largely stopped but flare-ups continue. The Middle East is expected on the agenda when Trump meets Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November.
summary: In the ninth month of the war, Iran's Revolutionary Guards targeted a US radar in Bahrain on 17 November, the US struck a missile site on Qeshm Island hours later, and Bahrain and Kuwait say they intercepted further drones. No casualties were reported in those attacks, but ships in and near the Strait of Hormuz keep being hit. Qatar and Oman are mediating; there is no peace deal.

conflicts: Iran says three tankers hit mines on 17 November; the US says it has cleared the main routes of mines. The reports read here do not confirm the mine strikes independently.
